messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: unusual auth heartbeat fanout observed from proxy pool prox-1 -> multiple regional relays. Rate + fanout spike detected, potential session scraping. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/auth-fanout. Please ack and triage.

ops-oncall: acked. I'm on it, pulling logs now. Any immediate customer impact noted?

maya: seeing repeated short-lived requests (2–5s) from ~120 distinct IPs hitting /v1/session/validate with valid-looking tokens. Traffic started 00:02 UTC. Burst sustained ~90s.

samir: logs show KV-cache growth on session-store with s3-log-forwarder reporting write errors at 00:03. Could be health-check fanout plus bad retries.

leo: rolling a quick mitigation: enabling strict per-source rate limit on proxy layer and injecting a drop rule for the worst offenders. Applying WAF rule to block signature pattern X.

ops-oncall: please post exact commands so SREs can verify.

leo: command to add edge rate-limit (edgectl):
```
edgectl rate-limit add --name "hb-multipath-615987" --match-path "/v1/session/validate" --limit 50r/m --action block
```
Applied to prox-1/reg1.

maya: stopped the largest IP clusters at the edge. Traffic down ~65%. KV growth paused.

samir: important note — some requests contained legacy service tokens from svc-deploy-legacy that are bound to Dedicated pools for a handful of enterprise customers. Need to check if tokens were replayed externally.

ops-oncall: grabbing the token audit. If confirmed, we'll need immediate service-account rotation for svc-deploy-legacy. Who owns rotation? @sre-rotations?

sre-rotations: on it. Preparing rotation plan. Short plan: 1) revoke current keys for svc-deploy-legacy, 2) generate new keys, 3) update dedicated pool pinning config with new key, 4) notify impacted customers on delay window. Aim TTR 12–18 minutes for internal rollout, customer windows vary.

eng-infra: before revoking, we should snapshot who has pinned tokens to avoid customer outages. Query: `SELECT customer_id FROM dedicated_pins WHERE svc_account='svc-deploy-legacy';` Running now.

cust-support: please flag any customers who have active pinned tokens. We'll prep CSM messages if rollout affects them.

maya: quick grep of logs shows header pattern `X-Env: staging` on ~7% of requests — looks like a misrouted staging forwarder is amplifying health checks. Recommend disabling log-forwarder stream `staging-proxy-debug-3` until we scrub.

leo: disabling stream now: `logctl disable --stream staging-proxy-debug-3` -> done. Error volume dropped further.

samir: however, a subset of logs were shipped to an S3 bucket with lifecycle set to public-read for a short window historically (old infra misconfig). Need to confirm whether any auth headers landed there.

ops-oncall: listing recent objects to check for headers:
```
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-staging-logs/proxy/2026/05/ --recursive --human-readable --summarize
```
Found objects at 00:02-00:05 UTC.

maya: grepping object contents for "Authorization" shows a handful of matches. Likely third-party indexer logs contain header snippets.

legal: if auth headers or tokens are in S3 and were public-readable, we need to treat as potential credential exposure. Start containment and we will assess disclosure obligations.

ops-oncall: containment steps executed: 1) disabled forwarding (leo), 2) edge rate-limits (leo), 3) isolated affected S3 prefix and changed bucket ACL to private and revoked public policies: `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-staging-logs --acl private`

samir: next: rotate svc-deploy-legacy keys immediately for safety and rotate any customer-visible service tokens we control. For dedicated customers with pinned creds, we need a targeted key rotation and a short maintenance window.

sre-rotations: initiating rotation for svc-deploy-legacy now. Generating new key pair, pushing to secret-manager, and deploying to dedicated controller with canary to 2 small customers first.

eng-infra: customers pinned: cust-zenith, cust-parable, cust-lumen. Notifying cust-support to prepare messages.

cust-support: assembling templates. ETA 8 min.

ops-oncall: also starting token revocation audit: `authctl audit --service svc-deploy-legacy --since 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z --fields token_id,customer_id,ip`

maya: initial audit shows ~40 token_ids used in spike; 6 belong to pinned customers. We'll avoid blind revocation for pinned ones until we coordinate with account owners.

legal: preserve evidence, log chain-of-custody. Legal wants a digest of which objects had headers and which customers potentially affected.

sre-rotations: rotation done for svc-deploy-legacy internal (non-pinned) consumers. Confirmed deployment to hosted runtime. Update: no customer-facing errors in canary.

leo: applying deploy to dedicated controllers for pinned customers with scheduled short window. Plan: push new key -> enable dual-key acceptance for 5 min -> revoke old key. That should minimize downtime.

ops-oncall: dual-key acceptance enabled.

samir: we should scrub the S3 objects before any retention — running scrub and redact job now: `log-scrub --bucket redwood-staging-logs --prefix proxy/2026/05/ --pattern "Authorization" --action redact`

ops-oncall: redact job completed. Created immutable journal of redaction operations for legal.

cust-support: drafted message: "We detected unusual traffic that may have included legacy tokens in logs. We rotated internal keys and are coordinating with you if your environment uses pinned tokens. No confirmed customer-level compromise detected at this time." Want legal sign-off.

legal: reviewed. Minor edits, OK to send to affected customers after rotation completes.

ops-oncall: rotation for pinned customers in progress (cust-zenith, cust-parable, cust-lumen). Tracking rollout IDs: r-615987-1, r-615987-2, r-615987-3.

maya: monitoring: no error spikes. Traffic normalized. Auth-rate stable.

sre-rotations: rotation complete for all pinned customers. Old keys revoked. Confirmed no service degradation post-switch.

ops-oncall: closing immediate containment. Opening internal ticket RED-INC-20260515-001 with timeline and artifacts. Assigning to infra sec squad for follow-up.

legal: prepping incident report and timeline for regulators if needed.

cust-support: sending customer notifications now (templates with legal-approved verbiage).

samir: postmortem owners: eng-infra + infra-sec + ops. Recommend follow-ups: 1) harden log-forwarder ACLs and add a pre-deploy policy check, 2) ensure no public ACLs for staging buckets, 3) add a token leak detection eval to Optimize to flag header dumps.

ops-oncall: thumbs up. I'll leave a handoff to night oncall at 00:30 UTC. @leo please drop a short summary for the handover.

leo: TL;DR for next oncall: heartbeat fanout caused staging forwarder amplification -> some auth headers found in staging S3 objects -> forwarder disabled, S3 ACL fixed, tokens rotated (internal + pinned customers), logs redacted, customers notified. Monitor for replays and any user reports.

ops-oncall: thanks everyone. Incident status -> mitigated. Will convert to postmortem and link once ticket created. :white_check_mark:
